description: independent non-Warsaw two-leg LM refit of the signature-bearing LPC 1902-1950 cohort (step_127 machinery); the carrier-degeneracy close on the objects that carry the anomaly
verdict: SIGNATURE-COHORT REPLICATION: the independent two-leg refit concords with the catalogue per-comet rotations (rho=1.000, n=17) and reproduces the in-cap excess on identical members (refit MWU p=0.0409, median-gap permutation p=0.069; catalogue p=0.0409).  The historical carrier is a feature of the raw astrometry, not of the Warsaw fit products.  Shared astrometry and a standard force model bound interpretation; the fitted subset is small and set by observability.
caveats: Thirteen of the thirty LPCs fail the same per-leg observation floor applied uniformly to every cohort (MIN_OBS_LEG = 12, MIN_LEG_SPAN_D = 5 d): early-century astrometry is sparse, so the fittable subset is set by observability, not by selection on the anomaly.
The dual-leg subset (T3) is small on this cohort; the decisive channel here is the per-comet rotation record (T1+T2), which the single-leg-fittable members carry.
